Q: VBA/Regex replace characters with groups using pattern A:

I fixed your macro, try it

Your regex was perfect! You just needed to add cell.NumberFormat = "@" before assigning the new value. Without it, Excel reconverts "7:30AM" back to time format and displays it as "7:30:00 AM" again.

Sub Trim()
    Dim cvold As String
    Dim cvnew As String
    Dim RX As Object
    
    Set RX = CreateObject("VBScript.RegExp")
    With RX
        .Global = False
        .IgnoreCase = True
        .Pattern = "(\d{1,2}:\d{2}):00 ([AP]M)"
    End With
    
    For Each cell In Selection
        cvold = cell.Text  ' Better to use .Text instead of .Value
        cvnew = RX.Replace(cvold, "$1$2")
        cell.NumberFormat = "@"  ' THIS LINE WAS MISSING! Format as text before assigning
        cell.Value = cvnew
    Next cell
End Sub

Q: Make single array outside for loop in PHP A:

Fundamentally, your script suffers from overwriting data on each iteration of the loop.

For a most-minimal edit, you could push rows this way:

$total[] = ['taxiNumber' => $i, 'status' => $querys->num_rows() ? 'booked' : 'available'];

However, the above would be a bandaid solution that doesn't address the bad practice of making iterated queries. One step better would be to refactor the method to avoid looped queries.

I'll populate a derived table with UNION ALL as done here.

public function getUserTaxiChairStatuses(int $userId): array
{
    $maxSeats = $this->db
        ->get_where('taxiInfo', ['userId' => $userId])
        ->row('totalTaxi');

    if (!$maxSeats) {
        return [];
    }

    return $this->db
        ->select('seats.num seat')
        ->select("CASE WHEN b.id IS NULL THEN 'available' ELSE 'booked' END status")
        ->join(
            '(' . implode(' UNION ALL ', substr_replace(['1 num'] + range(1, $maxSeats), 'SELECT ', 0, 0)) . ') seats',
            'seats.num <= t.totalTaxi'
        )
        ->join(
            'booking b',
            'b.userId = t.userId AND b.taxiNumber = seats.num AND b.servicedate = CURDATE()',
            'left'
        )
        ->get_where('taxiInfo t', ['t.userId => $userId])
        ->result();
}

The above refactored method will return an array of zero or more object with properties named seat and status.

The rendered SQL of the second query is:

SELECT `seats`.`num` `seat`, CASE WHEN b.id IS NULL THEN 'available' ELSE 'booked' END status
FROM `taxiInfo` `t`
JOIN (SELECT 1 num UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3) seats ON `seats`.`num` <= `t`.`totalTaxi`
LEFT JOIN `booking` `b` ON `b`.`userId` = `t`.`userId` AND `b`.`taxiNumber` = `seats`.`num` AND `b`.`servicedate` = CURDATE()
WHERE `t`.`userId` = 2

Ultimately, if you have control over the schema, it would be better to represent sets as individual rows instead of a count. This would allow you to make a single JOIN clause and remove the clunky derived table.

Q: How to list variables declared in script in bash? A:

Not sure when bash learned this but it's been a while: declare -p prints only variables unless you ask for functions instead and uses the escaped $' format for any value including control characters like newlines or whatever.

So

declare -p >.startup-vars
your stuff here
declare -p | diff -u .startup-vars - | sed -n '/^@/,${s/^+//p}'

looks pretty much bulletproof, it preserves all attributes and any multiline or otherwise weird values. Extending it to also replicate unsets seems straightforward enough.

Q: subclass of str fails subclass of list works .. why? A:

So, there is no str.__init__. The str class doesn't implement any __init__, and thus, super() calls object.__init__.

Your example seems like a toy example. There is no need to override __init__ in either of your examples since your implementation simply calls the super-class __init__. Really, the implementation shouldn't override __init__ at all.

For immutable types, if you want to intercept object construction, you must override __new__ if that is your intention in your actual code.

Just figured out this bloomberg API:

One can use =BDP("ticker","field") to download the company names.

For example, ESS PW Equity

And the field for company name is "NAME"

This gives :=BDP("ESS PW Equity","Name") company name.

Q: How can I read my app's database file from device? A:

You can view (visualize) the data in the .db file by using the software called "DB Browser for SQLITE"

  1. get your .db file from the device(smartphone) memory (by accessing the DDMS --> File explore)
  2. download and install sqlitebrowser (http://sqlitebrowser.org/)
  3. after installing, open "DB Browser for SQLITE" and go to "open database" to load your .db file
  4. Choose the "Browse data" tab
  5. Finally, select the table you want to visualize to display the data in the database.
